explanations: The bulk-write catch in productIndexer.ts wraps the error in an IndexingError but does not pass { cause: err }; it only copies the message into the text. isRetryable walks the cause chain with rootCause, so for these errors it sees the IndexingError itself, which is neither a SearchClusterError nor carries an errno code, and returns false. Transient 429/5xx responses and connection resets from the search cluster are therefore never retried, and batches are marked failed on the first hiccup. The catalog-load wrapper above it passes the cause correctly.

The catalog wrapper passes { cause: err }, so rootCause follows .cause back to the errno error and isRetryable returns true for ETIMEDOUT; with attempt 1 < 4 the job sleeps and retries. The wrapper's own lack of a code does not matter because the root is checked, errors are caught per batch rather than aborting, and attempt increments in the for loop up to MAX_ATTEMPTS.

seen is local to each call and records every error visited; if a cause chain loops back on itself the while condition fails and the walk stops. It does not touch logging or persist between calls, and stopping at non-Error causes is done by the instanceof Error check, not by the set.

The condition res.status >= 300 || res.body?.errors is true, so SearchClusterError(…, 200) is thrown inside the same try, and the catch below wraps it in an IndexingError. It is not counted as indexed, the client returned normally, and there is no per-document fallback.
